**(B)** Flamingo

A flamingo is a bird, and birds are uricotelic: they convert ammonia into uric acid, which saves water but costs the most energy. The polar bear (a mammal), the shark (a cartilaginous fish) and the adult frog are ureotelic, and making urea costs less energy than making uric acid.

**(D)** nucleic acids

Humans are ureotelic, so the nitrogen of excess amino acids leaves as urea, not uric acid. Uric acid in humans comes from breaking down the purine bases (adenine and guanine) of nucleic acids, which is why too much of it causes gout. Fatty acids contain no nitrogen, and creatinine is itself a separate waste from muscle creatine phosphate.

[Note: the chapter does not state this; standard biology gives purine (nucleic acid) breakdown as the source of uric acid in humans.]

**(D)** Cells with brush border

The visceral layer of Bowman's capsule is made of special cells, the podocytes, so the pair links a part of the nephron with its characteristic lining cells. The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by cuboidal cells bearing a brush border of microvilli, which greatly increases the area for reabsorption. Ciliated cells line the neck, and squamous cells line the descending limb of Henle's loop.

**(A)** Bowman's capsule

Ultrafiltration forces plasma, minus its proteins, out of the glomerular capillaries into the capsular space of Bowman's capsule. This glomerular filtrate is called deproteinised plasma or primary urine. The glomerular capillaries still hold whole blood with its proteins, and by the time the fluid reaches the limbs of Henle's loop it has been changed by reabsorption in the PCT.

**(B)** increases

ADH makes the walls of the last part of the DCT and the collecting duct permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed. The urine becomes smaller in volume and more concentrated, and a more concentrated urine has a higher specific gravity.

**(A)** Urination

Micturition is the expulsion of urine from the urinary bladder through the urethra, a reflex under conscious control of the external sphincter. Urine formation is the work of the nephrons, uremia is a rise of urea in the blood above 0.05%, and urolithiasis is the formation of kidney stones.

As printed, two options are correct: the chapter counts protonephridia as nephridia, so the liver fluke qualifies as well as the earthworm.

The earthworm excretes through metanephridia, coiled tubes that open into the body cavity by a nephrostome and to the outside by a nephridiopore; this is the answer the question means. But the liver fluke is a flatworm (Platyhelminthes), and the chapter lists protonephridia, networks of flame cells, as the other major type of nephridia, found mostly in Platyhelminthes. The cockroach uses Malpighian tubules and the crab uses green glands, so neither has nephridia. Had the question said "metanephridia", the earthworm would be the single answer.

**(C)** oxalic acid

The commonest kidney stones are calcium oxalate stones. Tomatoes contain oxalic acid (oxalate), which can combine with calcium in the urine and add to such stones, so patients are told to avoid them. The seeds, the red pigment lycopene and the sour taste are not what forms stones.

[Note: the chapter does not state this; standard biology gives tomatoes as an oxalate-rich food.]

**(D)** Henle's loop

The loop of Henle concentrates the medulla by moving water out of the descending limb and NaCl out of the ascending limb; it is a site of reabsorption, not of secretion. The DCT and the collecting duct actively secrete creatinine, \(\text{K}^+\) and \(\text{H}^+\) into the urine, and the PCT also secretes \(\text{H}^+\), ammonia and some drugs.

[Note: the chapter does not state this; standard biology gives tubular secretion in the PCT, DCT and collecting duct, but not in the loop of Henle.]

**(A)** collects urine

Each renal papilla, the tip of a pyramid, opens into a minor calyx, which collects the urine from it. Minor calyces join into major calyces, and these form the renal pelvis, which is what continues as the ureter. The calyces lie in the renal sinus beside the medulla, not in the cortex, and the columns of Bertini are cortical tissue lying between the pyramids.

**(B)** Malpighian tubule

Malpighian tubules are the blind-ended excretory tubules of insects such as the cockroach. The human kidney has Malpighian bodies (renal corpuscles), each made of a glomerulus inside Bowman's capsule, and nephrons with a loop of Henle.

**(C)** urochrome

Normal urine is pale yellow because of the pigment urochrome, formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin. Urea and uric acid are colourless nitrogenous wastes, and cholesterol is not a normal constituent of urine.

**(C)** LoH

The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water but pumps \(\text{Na}^+\) and \(\text{Cl}^-\) out, so the filtrate becomes progressively more dilute as it climbs and leaves the loop hypotonic to blood. In the PCT the filtrate stays isotonic, and in the DCT and collecting tubule water is withdrawn under ADH, concentrating the urine.

**(A)** cloaca

In reptiles the urine passes from the kidneys into the cloaca, where water is reabsorbed and the uric acid collects as a semi-solid white paste until it is voided along with the faeces. Fat bodies are where insects such as the cockroach store uric acid, the liver makes nitrogenous wastes but does not store them, and the anus is only an opening.

[Note: the chapter does not state this; standard biology gives the cloaca as the place where reptiles hold uric acid before voiding it.]

**(B)** proximal tubule

The proximal convoluted tubule is the main site of selective reabsorption: its brush-border cells actively take back high-threshold substances such as glucose, amino acids, vitamin C and ions. The loop of Henle, DCT and collecting tubule mainly handle water and salts and carry out secretion.

**(A)** cortex

The renal cortex contains the Malpighian bodies (glomerulus plus Bowman's capsule), the convoluted tubules and blood vessels, which gives it its granular look. The medulla, arranged as pyramids, holds mainly the loops of Henle and collecting ducts, and the pelvis is the funnel that collects urine.

**(D)** uricotelic

Desert snakes must save as much water as possible, so they excrete nitrogen as uric acid, which is least toxic and least soluble and needs almost no water to be removed. Ammonia needs a large amount of water and urea a moderate amount, and "aminotelic" (excreting amino acids) is not the mode of a desert reptile.

**(B)** amino acids

Excess amino acids cannot be stored, so they are deaminated in the liver: the amino group is removed as ammonia, which the ornithine (urea) cycle turns into urea. Fatty acids, fats and glucose contain no nitrogen, so they cannot give rise to urea.

**(C)** both a and b

ADH increases water reabsorption from the last part of the DCT and the collecting duct, reducing the volume of urine. Aldosterone, released through the renin-angiotensin system, makes the DCT and collecting ducts reabsorb more \(\text{Na}^+\) and water, which also reduces urine volume. Both hormones therefore regulate how much urine is passed.
